subject.title: fix(scripts): warn when postinstall detects running gateway with stale module imports

question: Should direct npm or package-manager installs probe local Gateway state during postinstall, or should stale-Gateway warnings remain owned by the updater and managed-service lifecycle?
rationale: Both approaches can mitigate the reported failure, but only maintainers can decide whether every applicable package install may perform a network probe and whether the new environment-variable contract is warranted.

options.title: Narrow postinstall fallback
options.body: Keep direct rollback and reinstall coverage, but remove the new opt-out variable and minimize the probe and port-resolution contract before merge.

options.title: Updater lifecycle only
options.body: Use the restart-skipped updater warning path from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99330 and leave raw package-manager installs outside managed restart handling.

options.title: Accept proposed behavior
options.body: Merge the current hook while explicitly owning the install delay, possible false-positive warnings, duplicated port resolution, and opt-out variable.

recommendation.title: Narrow postinstall fallback
recommendation.body: Keep direct rollback and reinstall coverage, but remove the new opt-out variable and minimize the probe and port-resolution contract before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged generation-retention work provides the strongest current-main ownership evidence for the stale-import mitigation boundary.
